identity.name: SANSERA ENGINEERING LTD
identity.industry: Precision Engineering & Strategic Manufacturing for Aerospace, Semiconductors & xEV

summary.oneLiner: Sansera delivered record Q4 revenue and margin expansion driven by ADS (aerospace/semiconductor) growth and auto ICE resilience, with order book visibility of INR44.6B over 5 years and capex planned to scale capacity for high-margin segments — what matters is the structural shift from auto-centric to diversified high-value manufacturing with semiconductor and aerospace as new growth pillars.

one-line thesis: Sansera delivered record Q4 revenue and margin expansion driven by ADS (aerospace/semiconductor) growth and auto ICE resilience, with order book visibility of INR44.6B over 5 years and capex planned to scale capacity for high-margin segments — what matters is the structural shift from auto-centric to diversified high-value manufacturing with semiconductor and aerospace as new growth pillars.
financial scorecard: revenue: +28% YoY to INR9,987cr; EBITDA/margin: +52% YoY to INR1,929cr, margin +306bps to 19.3%; PAT (rptd): +108% YoY to INR1,231cr, margin 12.3% (vs 7.6%); PAT (normalized): exclude INR172cr forex gain → PAT ~INR1,059cr; order book: INR44.6B cumulative 5-year backlog (ADS); net debt: INR3,972cr cash position, net debt negative
guidance: revenue growth: target INR8,000–10,000cr by decade-end; margin: ADS margin to reach 25–30% at full utilization; order inflow: expect recovery in Q2–Q3 FY27; capex/commissioning: FY27 capex ~INR5,100cr (same as FY26), including INR250cr for ADS, INR50cr JV, new Pantnagar/Manesar plants, land acquisition near airport
order book & pipeline: INR44.6B cumulative 5-year unexecuted order backlog (primarily ADS); peak annual new business revenue at INR19.2B as of March 2026
segment / subsidiary detail: Auto ICE: INR6,426cr Q4 (+21.6% YoY); xEV/Tech-Agnostic: INR1,217cr Q4 (+19.8% YoY); ADS: INR1,736cr Q4 (+70.5% YoY, >2x YOY); Semiconductor: outperformed expectations (zero base growth); Aerospace: grew 63.3% YoY; Defense: strong from small base; 2-wheeler: +29.9% YoY (Bajaj), +13.3% YoY (TVS); MHCV: limited to Daimler/Volvo Eicher; JV with Nichidai targeting driveline/steering forged components
growth verticals / optionality: Semiconductor: scaling with AI-driven demand; Aerospace: winning complex blisk, engine casing, structural parts; Defense: new programs; Energy Storage: INR80–100cr/year program with potential for more; Hybrid ICE: expanding component offerings; International expansion: U.S. plant discussions re-energized post-tariff reduction
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 19.3% (Q4) on product mix shift to higher-margin ADS; cost pressures: steel, aluminum, energy, tooling, freight; automation reducing labor dependency (80% robotic lines on new lines); semiconductor margins 'super exciting' but constrained by machine lead times (7–9 months)
capex / expansion: FY26: INR5,097cr; FY27: ~INR5,100cr; breakdown: INR250cr ADS expansion, INR50cr Nichidai JV (forging press procured), Plant 6/12 forging/machining upgrades, new Manesar facility, 10-acre land near airport for future ADS
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for ADS, forging, automation; maintaining negative net debt (INR3,972cr cash); no dividend policy mentioned; JV investment aligned with strategic diversification; no share buyback or M&A mentioned
risks & watch-items: Global tariff volatility (esp. U.S.); inflation in steel/aluminum/energy; machine tool lead times (7–9 months) constraining semiconductor growth; geopolitical disruptions; labor shortage in skilled machining; execution risk on new ADS/semiconductor ramps
management quality / tone: Highly confident, bullish on ADS/semiconductor/aerospace; emphasis on operational excellence, automation, and capacity building; cautious on macro but not on structural tailwinds; proactive on land acquisition and JV execution; tone reflects strategic discipline and long-term vision
non-obvious takeaways: 1. Sansera is now India’s only player with capability to machine aerospace blisks (rotating engine parts) — a global rarity; 2. Semiconductor growth is not just EMS but high-value, high-margin precision machined components; 3. 80% automation on new lines reduces labor dependency — a rare edge in Indian manufacturing; 4. Land acquisition near airport signals intent to become aerospace supply chain anchor; 5. INR19.2B peak annual new business revenue implies 55%+ CAGR potential over next 3 years

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
